text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and automated builds start immediately. This means the software is compiled and checked without anyone doing it by hand. As part of the build, the team also runs tests to make sure everything works correctly. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear process. One of the main benefits is catching issues early, before they become big problems. When bugs are found quickly, they are easier and cheaper to fix. As a result, teams can release better software faster and with more confidence.
